clue.text: Basketball manoeuvre in back street, hoop lacking height

parts.note: an alley is a narrow back street

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is dropped from the word hoop

explanation.surface: A basketball player shoots at a hoop in a back alley, perhaps one with no headroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley-oop is a basketball play where one player lobs the ball for a teammate to catch in mid-air and dunk.

clue.text: Gangster wanting to fence fine article

indicators.note: to fence is to enclose, so the outer word surrounds the others

parts.note: wanting in the sense of lacking or in short supply, i.e. scarce
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A criminal is looking to sell on a fine piece through a fence, a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like the criminal's receiver of stolen goods; here 'to fence' means to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone and the title of famous films about mobsters.

clue.text: Satisfy publican, at first, with tenancy agreement

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of publican

parts.note: a lease is a contract letting property to a tenant

explanation.surface: A landlord's needs are met by a decent tenancy agreement for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to gratify or content them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A Brie I distributed in part of Europe

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands out portions of brie cheese in some European region.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, in south-west Europe.

clue.text: Man in charge, supported by a church

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means placed beneath the preceding pieces

parts.note: Basil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in charge of something is propped up by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large church of a particular oblong design, often given special papal privileges.

clue.text: This person's crimson on the outside, with unknown cure

indicators.note: on the outside says the colour word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red
this person is the setter, i.e. me; the 's is 'is', a link
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to being red-faced, having found a mysterious cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter speaking of themself, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals an illness, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Serving US soldier in one's pub is sensible

indicators.note: in says the soldier sits inside the pub word

parts.note: your local is the pub nearest home that you frequent
a GI is an enlisted soldier in the American army

explanation.surface: Having an American serviceman drinking in your local pub is a reasonable arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logical follows reason, so it is sensible; a near synonym.

clue.text: Blood surrounding head of goat in ravine

indicators.note: surrounding says the blood word wraps around the following letter

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: head of picks only the opening letter of goat

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene: a goat's head lies in blood at the bottom of a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley, a synonym for ravine.

clue.text: Shake unruly child in the course of struggle

indicators.note: in the course of means during, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A tantrum-throwing child shakes while fighting against restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to quiver or tremble rapidly, a synonym for shake as a verb.

clue.text: Screen concealing it, migratory bird

indicators.note: concealing says the screen word hides the other piece within it

parts.note: a visor is a shield or screen for the eyes

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's hide conceals a passing bird on migration.
explanation.definitionFit: Birders call a species that arrives for a season only a summer or winter visitor.

clue.text: Alarm losing time causes miscalculation

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the alarm word

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or alarm

explanation.surface: An alarm clock that runs slow leads someone to get their timing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarm' looks like a clock, but means fright.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, and a miscalculation is one kind of mistake.

clue.text: Firm: it's averse to change

indicators.note: to change means to alter, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A company announces it resists any change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a noun, a company; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertive person is forthright and resolute, so firm in manner.

clue.text: Kind of household to arrange tea for men in play

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Someone organises a tea for the cast of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A home headed by a single mother or father is the type of household described.

clue.text: Have groups of searchers on face of Snowdon

parts.note: posses are bands of people searching, as in westerns

indicators.note: face of takes the front letter of Snowdon

explanation.surface: Search parties are combing the face of Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, a synonym for have.

clue.text: Make clear power must be cloaked in betrayal

indicators.note: cloaked in says the letter is wrapped inside the betrayal word

parts.note: a sellout is a betrayal of principles or people
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A warning that the powerful must disguise their treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell out is to explain explicitly and in detail, an idiom for clarify.

clue.text: Son, wizard scout

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Harry Potter is the famous boy wizard

explanation.surface: A boy who is a wizard joins the Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter is a lookout who watches for something, just as a scout does.

clue.text: Stop female artist wearing check

indicators.note: wearing says the check word is worn around the other pieces

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman painter in a checked outfit is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like a pattern being worn, but means restrain. RA (Royal Academician) is a convention for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, a synonym for stop.

clue.text: Until we meet again, get on with the Spanish and Latin

parts.note: to fare is to get on, as in how did you fare?
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A parting wish for someone getting along with Spanish and Latin studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is a parting word, said as one leaves until another meeting.

clue.text: Unnecessary enmity on steamship

parts.note: needle is British slang for hostility or rivalry, as in a needle match

explanation.surface: Pointless feuding breaks out aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDLE in British usage means bad feeling between rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, a synonym for unnecessary.

clue.text: Small scone unfinished, dunked in cup of tea in notable meeting

indicators.note: dunked in says the small items are dipped inside the cup word

parts.note: one's cup of tea is what one likes, a preference

indicators.note: unfinished drops the closing letter of scone

explanation.surface: A dignified gathering where someone dips a little scone into a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup of tea' is an idiom: something that is your cup of tea is to your taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is a meeting at which a public figure briefs journalists.

clue.text: Father, smart in church government

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
smart in the sense of brisk or quick, i.e. pacy

explanation.surface: A well-dressed priest takes part in running the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like well-dressed but means brisk.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office and governing authority of the Pope over the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Move at home to intervene

parts.note: a step is a move
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone moves in at home in order to intervene in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is an idiom for getting involved to settle a situation.

clue.text: Woodland in east in grip of nasty frost

indicators.note: in grip of says the letter is held inside the rearranged letters
nasty indicates the word frost is roughed up into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Woodland in the east of the country gripped by a harsh frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges FROST into FORST; 'in grip of' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area covered with trees, i.e. woodland.

clue.text: Relative of Connie Cezon

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters lie inside Connie Cezon

explanation.surface: A query about a family member of someone called Connie Cezon.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, so a family relative.

clue.text: Synthetic fibre made by college, girl heard

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of college

indicators.note: heard says the name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Esther is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A student at college talks about a girl's synthetic clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY is short for polytechnic, a former type of British college.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a man-made fibre widely used in clothing.

clue.text: Turn scoundrel going after wife

indicators.note: going after places the scoundrel word behind the letter

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A rogue changes direction and pursues someone's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round or pivot, a synonym.

clue.text: Messenger in hall of justice endlessly? That is right

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the court word

parts.note: a court is a hall where justice is administered
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A messenger delivering papers to a court asks whether they are in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is someone who carries packages or messages, a synonym.

clue.text: Joins servicemen after one goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing says a letter is taken out of the servicemen word

parts.note: soldiers are servicemen
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops sign up after a comrade goes missing in action.
explanation.definitionFit: To solder is to fuse metal parts with molten alloy, so joining them.
